items.title: Gobind: RM226bil in data centre investments to create more than 4,000 jobs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's 27 data centre projects approved under the Data Centre Task Force (DCTF), involving an estimated RM225.97 billion in investments, are expected to create 4,053 jobs. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said 3,523 of the positions would be highly skilled jobs, with most expected to be filled by Malaysians. Gobind said the positions would cover electrical and mechanical engineering, networking, cybersecurity, and data centre operations and maintenance.

items.title: MinDef enters cooperation with HR Ministry on veteran employment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Ministry of Defence (MinDef) is strengthening its commitment to the welfare and future of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel and veterans through the MyBakat Veteran initiative, which aims to benefit more than 15,000 people by 2030. Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the initiative underscores MinDef’s new approach to ensuring that MAF personnel receive support not only during their service but are also better prepared to pursue a second career after retirement. He said the ministry is placing greater emphasis on aligning military skills and experience with industry requirements to broaden job opportunities for MAF personnel and veterans.

items.title: BYD driver brought to court over fatal crash that killed 5-year-old girl [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The BYD Seal driver involved in a six-vehicle crash that killed a 5-year-old girl along Jalan Kuching on Saturday was brought to the court complex to face three charges. Her father sustained injuries to his right hand, while the 33-year-old Yamaha 135LC motorcyclist suffered head injuries. Police later located the BYD Seal driver at the private hospital.

items.title: Teenager's death: 14 suspects to be charged today
items.summary: GURUN: Fourteen suspects, including two minors, will be charged at the Gurun Court today over the death of a teenager whose body was found along Jalan Harvard here seven days ago. The 18-year-old victim was found by members of the public by the roadside with injuries to his head and face. At a previous press conference, Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said the teenager had been confined for two days, tortured and had his hair cut with scissors after being accused of stealing a motorcycle.

items.title: Zara Qairina inquest: Coroner concludes witness phase, to set final directions tomorrow
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 15 — The Coroner’s Court here today concluded hearing the testimonies of all 83 witnesses in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir, with Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan fixing Friday morning for further directions on submissions. Amir Shah, before adjourning today’s proceedings, said no further deponents would be called on Friday, with the court sitting at 9 am for directions on submissions in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina. On Aug 8, 2025, the AGC said that Zara Qairina’s remains would be exhumed to allow for a post-mortem examination.

items.title: EGH International eyes growth as RM313.5mil order book underpins ACE Market debut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: EGH International Bhd is banking on a RM313.5 million order book, improving margins and a stronger balance sheet to drive earnings growth as the interior fit-out specialist prepares to make its debut on the ACE Market. The research house forecasts EGH International to register core net earnings of RM12.3 million in the financial year ending March 2027 (FY27) and RM14.6 million in FY28. EGH International has more than 15 years of experience providing turnkey interior fit-out services, covering design, procurement, construction and installation.

items.title: Malaysia is building its own digital cloud to safeguard data sovereignty, minister says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The government is developing a sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) cloud to ensure the country’s classified information remains secure and beyond the reach of foreign laws and policies, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the initiative was crucial to protecting Malaysia’s digital sovereignty, particularly in securing sensitive government information, including official documents, that could be at risk if stored on public cloud services. Therefore, the government has decided to develop a sovereign AI cloud,” he said.

items.title: United Malacca's RM6.10 offer undervalues assets, says analyst
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: United Malacca Bhd's conditional mandatory general offer (MGO) at RM6.10 per share undervalues its plantation landbank and potential asset monetisation opportunities. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang described the offer as unattractive, noting that it represents a mere 2.2 per cent premium to United Malacca's closing price before the announcement. The MGO was triggered after Prosper Trading Sdn Bhd acquired Great Eastern Life Assurance (Malaysia) Bhd's 13.44 per cent stake in United Malacca for RM171.9 million, raising the offerors' combined shareholding to 47.66 per cent.

items.title: Religious minister urges joint Muslim prayers as ‘weapon’ against haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan has urged Muslims to perform solat hajat (special prayers) amid the haze affecting the country. In a Facebook post yesterday, Zulkifli called for the prayers to be performed simultaneously at all mosques and suraus in the Federal Territories. I urge that solat hajat be held simultaneously at all mosques and suraus in the Federal Territories.

items.title: Finance Ministry: RON97 down to RM5.10, diesel to RM5.17
items.summary: MOF said recipients of BUDI MADANI RON95 (BUDI95) would continue to pay RM1.99 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised RON95 price of RM4.62 per litre. The government would bear a subsidy of RM2.63 per litre, or 57 per cent of the unsubsidised price. Recipients of BUDI MADANI Diesel (BUDI Diesel) would continue to pay RM2.10 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised diesel price of RM5.17 per litre.

items.title: Big Tree launches Santuari Kita for mental well-being
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Big Tree, a Malaysian out-of-home (OOH) advertising solutions provider and a subsidiary of Media Prima Bhd, has launched Santuari Kita, a community-driven campaign to promote mental well-being. The campaign, under the Ruang Rehat initiative, supports World Mental Health Day and invites Malaysians to share messages of hope, encouragement and kindness. The messages will collectively build a digital garden symbolising compassion, resilience and emotional wellbeing.

items.title: Government agency chairman arrives in court to face land deal charges
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A government agency chairman with the title Datuk, who was arrested to assist investigations into the sale of eight plots of land below market value, arrived at the Sessions Court here today to face charges. At the time, the chairman was arrested alongside four others, namely his brother, sister-in-law and two company directors, during MACC operations in August. The MACC has obtained approval to charge the chairman today under Op Jurus.

items.title: Gold steadies after hitting one-week low
items.summary: LONDON: Gold prices were nearly steady on Thursday after touching a one-week low in the previous session as hot inflation data boosted expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate hike this month. US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.7 per cent to US$4,136.10. Among other metals, spot silver was up 0.2 per cent at US$55.72 per ounce, platinum fell 0.5 per cent to US$1,598.96 and palladium rose 0.6 per cent to US$1,100.25.

items.title: Klang, Johan Setia record highest API reading at 192
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 34 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today. Port Dickson and Tangkak recorded readings of 175, while Cheras recorded 173. Meanwhile, 34 areas recorded moderate API readings.

items.title: Japan's Nikkei tumbles as tech stocks hammered on US rate hike worries
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei share average slumped in early trading on Thursday, with technology stocks hit hard after hot US inflation figures sparked fears of higher interest rates. The tech-heavy Nikkei dropped 3.5 per cent as of 0021 GMT, while the broader Topix fell 1.9 per cent. The US Nasdaq Composite slumped 1.9 per cent on Wednesday.

items.title: Fahmi: Pakatan 95pc done with Melaka candidate talks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Discussions on the list of Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates for the Melaka state election are over 95 per cent complete, said PH Communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi, who is also communications minister, said PH has scheduled its candidate announcement for Oct 24, with the venue to be confirmed later. “ Meanwhile, Fahmi said the candidate announcement, originally scheduled for today, had been postponed to Oct 24 at the request of the Melaka PH leadership.

items.title: OpenAI alleges former employee took files on unreleased device to Apple
items.summary: ISTANBUL: OpenAI has accused a former employee who returned to Apple of taking more than 100 highly confidential files related to an unreleased device under development, according to a legal filing submitted Wednesday, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing The Wall Street Journal. The filing also alleges that the former employee presented OpenAI's product plans to Apple executives, including a vice president of operations in Asia. OpenAI claimed the information may have helped Apple advance its plans for AI-powered products, including smart home devices that it announced Tuesday.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Haze, electricity tariffs, and data centres
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Dewan Rakyat is expected to discuss several key issues today, including increases in domestic electricity tariffs, the economic value of data centre investments, aviation safety and the impact of haze on public health. Datuk Wan Hassan Mohd Ramli (PN-Dungun) will ask about the Youth and Sports Ministry’s assessment of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 at the Sepang International Circuit, covering the event’s effectiveness, operational preparedness, stakeholder coordination and proposed improvements. Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah) will ask about the Health Ministry’s measures to address the impact of haze on public health, including cooperation with the Department of Environment and relevant agencies to monitor air quality, issue health advisories, and protect vulnerable groups.

items.title: Special budget needed to appoint hostel wardens to curb bullying in boarding schools
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Special allocations should be provided for boarding schools to fund full-time wardens as part of efforts to strengthen student safety and curb bullying, said Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. He said a dedicated budget from the Education Ministry to appoint full-time wardens was important to ensure students could be monitored around the clock, particularly at night when most bullying cases in hostels were reported to occur. Asyraf, who pioneered the appointment of former military personnel as full-time wardens at Mara Junior Science Colleges (MRSM), said relying on teachers to supervise students after school hours was no longer sufficient, given their existing workload and limited ability to monitor students until the early hours of the morning.

items.title: Fed's Daly says rate hikes likely needed, but not urgently
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO:The Federal Reserve will probably need to increase short-term interest rates further to rein in too-high inflation, San Francisco Federal Reserve president Mary Daly said on Wednesday, but she signaled there is no need to do so at the US central bank's Oct 27-28 meeting. The Fed's policy rate is in the 3.75 per cent to four per cent range. "Definitely this data point suggests that the risk to inflation remains elevated," Daly said.

items.title: OpenAI alleges former employee took files on unreleased device to Apple
items.summary: ISTANBUL: OpenAI has accused a former employee who returned to Apple of taking more than 100 highly confidential files related to an unreleased device under development, according to a legal filing submitted on Wednesday, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing The Wall Street Journal. The filing also alleges that the former employee presented OpenAI's product plans to Apple executives, including a vice-president of operations in Asia. OpenAI claimed the information may have helped Apple advance its plans for AI-powered products, including smart home devices that it announced on Tuesday.

items.title: Woman seriously injured in Penang Bridge crash
items.summary: PRAI: A 45-year-old woman was seriously injured when two cars collided on the Penang Bridge heading towards Prai early today, causing one of the vehicles to overturn. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 3.49am about the accident at Km1.3 of the bridge. He said the woman sustained serious injuries to her head, legs and hands.

items.title: The budget beyond the budget
items.summary: Yet the deficit of the consolidated public sector is projected to widen from 6.0 to 7.0 per cent. Its consolidated public-sector account combines general government with nonfinancial public corporations. General government includes the federal government, state governments, local governments and federal statutory bodies.

items.title: Doing the right things and doing things right
items.summary: This distinction is captured in a well-known management principle: effectiveness is doing the right things, while efficiency is doing things right. Conversely, an organisation may identify the right opportunities but waste resources through poor execution. Doing the Right Things: The Importance of Effectiveness Doing the right things means selecting objectives, priorities and activities that contribute meaningfully to the organisation's purpose and long-term success.

items.title: Electricity tariffs, data centres and haze impact among key issues in Dewan Rakyat today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat is expected to discuss several key issues today, including increases in domestic electricity tariffs, the economic value of data centre investments, aviation safety and the impact of haze on public health. Datuk Wan Hassan Mohd Ramli (PN-Dungun) will ask about the Youth and Sports Ministry's assessment of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 at the Sepang International Circuit, covering the event's effectiveness, operational preparedness, stakeholder coordination and proposed improvements. Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah) will ask about the Health Ministry's measures to address the impact of haze on public health, including cooperation with the Department of Environment and relevant agencies to monitor air quality, issue health advisories, and protect vulnerable groups.

items.title: Irene Sofiya murder: Classmate to be charged today [WATCH]
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A Form Four student will be charged in the magistrate's court today with murdering 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal at a hall in a secondary school in Yong Peng on Oct 3. Irene Sofiya, affectionately known as Fiya, was found unconscious and covered in blood at a school hall in Yong Peng at about 5.50pm before she was pronounced dead. The search ended when her friend found Fiya lying inside the school hall.

items.title: Israel ex-security chief sues Netanyahu for Oct 7 defamation
items.summary: JERUSALEM: The former head of Israel's Shin Bet domestic security agency sued Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for defamation on Wednesday, weeks before elections, in a row over responsibility for Hamas's Oct 7, 2023, attack. In the 134-page court document, Bar accused Netanyahu of "lying to cover himself" and said it was slanderous to accuse him of "criminal failures" over the attack. Bar is seeking three million shekels (around US$968,500) in damages from Netanyahu.

items.title: Trump's new press secretary faces scrutiny over credentials
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The White House was facing mounting questions on Wednesday over new press secretary Katie Zacharia's legal credentials, after a faltering first day in the job when she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam. "The State Bar should investigate whether Ms. Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials," she added. "I practised international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials," Zacharia said in a statement to AFP, without clarifying whether she held a US law licence.

items.title: Trump says he wants to see Pope 'get well'
items.summary: BULLHEAD CITY: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that he wanted to see Pope Leo XIV "get well" after the pontiff underwent surgery in Rome this week to remove a cancerous tumour. "I want to see Pope Leo get well," Trump told reporters after addressing a campaign rally in Arizona. You know, they're big Trump supporters," Trump said, adding: "His brother loves him a lot, loves the Pope a lot, and that's good.

items.title: Defence Ministry opens second career path for veterans
items.summary: Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the initiative underscores the ministry's new approach to ensuring that personnel receive support not only during their service but are also better prepared to pursue a second career after retirement. He said the ministry is placing greater emphasis on aligning military skills and experience with industry requirements to broaden job opportunities for its personnel and veterans. Defence secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali and human resources secretary-general Datuk Azman Mohd Yusof signed the Note of Cooperation in the presence of Khaled and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.

items.title: Regulate, tax 'Ali Baba' deals instead of criminalising them, economist says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will table new legislation or amend laws to curb "Ali Baba" practices and rent-seeking, but an economist believes regulating such practices would make more sense. Williams Business Consultancy Sdn Bhd founder and director Dr Geoffrey Williams said it would make no economic sense to criminalise Ali Baba practices as making them legal would allow them to be regulated and taxed while adding value to the economy. He said no money was lost through the practice of Malaysians subletting licences and concessions to foreigners.

items.title: Refugees should not be confined to 3D jobs, says NGO
items.summary: North South Initiative executive director Adrian Pereira said refugees should have the freedom to choose employment based on their skills, qualifications, capabilities and preferences, rather than being confined to low-skilled or demanding work. "Expanding employment opportunities for refugees should go beyond filling vacancies in sectors facing labour shortages. "The right to work must include the right to choose," he said.

items.title: Tighter scrapyard checks needed to tackle cable theft, says Bukit Aman [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police will conduct licence or permit inspections at scrap metal yards to cut off the market for stolen copper and cripple cable theft syndicates operating across the country. Federal police believe continuous checks at scrapyards are key to address the growing problem, particularly thefts involving telecommunications cables. Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Seri Noor Hisam Nordin said tackling cable theft required authorities to go beyond catching thieves in the act.

items.title: When home becomes a work problem [WATCH]
items.summary: A fall down the stairs, a road crash or even a cat bite can take a worker away from the job - and expose how an accident outside the workplace can still hit the household's finances, writes Intan Maizura Ahmad Kamal For most workers, a workplace accident is easy enough to picture: a fall at a construction site, an injury involving machinery, a collision while making a delivery. In its first three months, Perkeso recorded 6,330 claims under the scheme, with RM9.97 million in benefits paid out. Other claims involved road accidents and incidents during workers' personal time.

items.title: How Malaysia can raise its retirement age from 60 to 65: Experts explain the math and more
items.summary: Currently, Malaysia’s minimum retirement age of 60 means private sector employees are protected from premature retirement before 60, while civil servants have a mandatory retirement age of 60. However, global pension expert William Price said Malaysia needs to gradually increase its retirement age to at least 65 as Malaysians are living longer. He said “it’s very strange that Malaysia’s retirement age has been so low for so long” when many other countries had increased theirs.

items.title: Victims' kin get loan moratorium
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The families of 54 Malaysians still missing after the Nepal floods have secured a six-month loan moratorium, easing financial pressure amid uncertainty over their loved ones. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) coordinator and spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said HSBC and Public Bank confirmed the relief in writing following discussions with Bank Negara Malaysia on Oct 12. MASFIH said the families still faced financial commitments and unresolved legal questions while hoping for their loved ones' safe return.

items.title: Mohamad: Malaysians in Saudi Arabia safe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysians in Riyadh are safe and have not been affected by Houthi attacks, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said the ministry were receiving daily reports from the Malaysian embassy in Riyadh and consulate in Jeddah on the safety and welfare of Malaysians in Saudi Arabia. "The embassy is in contact with Malaysians in the country to ensure their welfare and safety," Mohamad said.

items.title: Trial defence says Russia used Nord Stream pipelines as 'weapon'
items.summary: HAMBURG: A lawyer for a Ukrainian accused of blowing up the Nord Stream pipelines supplying Russian gas to western Europe said on Wednesday that Moscow had used the network to exert political and economic pressure, as the former military officer's trial opened in Germany. The 50-year-old is accused of leading a Ukrainian team of divers and an explosives expert to bomb Nord Stream, seven months after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. He also accused Russia of using the pipelines as a political and economic "weapon".

items.title: Haze: Education Ministry coordinating school operating procedures under new action plan
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has begun coordinating school operating procedures based on the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) to ensure that decisions on school closures are made in a more systematic manner, taking into account Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and health advice. Its minister, Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, said that under the coordinated procedures, outdoor activities would be postponed when the API reading exceeds 100, while schools would be closed when the reading exceeds 200, in accordance with the PTJK. “Closing schools several days in advance without taking these changes into account could result in children losing learning time even after air quality has returned to normal,” she said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: PM Anwar extends donation to Makkal Osai senior editor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 (Bernama) — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended a donation to Makkal Osai senior editor Rajan Boopalan, who is undergoing treatment at Selayang Hospital after suffering a blood clot in his head. Anwar said several officers from the Prime Minister’s Office had visited Rajan at the hospital on his behalf. He also prayed for Rajan’s speedy recovery and for his treatment to proceed smoothly.

items.title: Malay Rulers urge outsiders not to politicise Negeri Sembilan throne dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 —The Malay Rulers have urged outsiders not to interfere in or politicise the dispute over the Negeri Sembilan throne, calling for the matter to be resolved by the relevant authorities through proper legal and customary channels. In a statement issued today by Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad on behalf of the Malay Rulers, all parties involved were urged to exercise wisdom, patience and respect for adab, adat and the dignity of the royal institution. As efforts to resolve the dispute continue, the Malay Rulers urged all parties to preserve family ties, social harmony and respect for the royal institution while avoiding statements or actions that could aggravate tensions.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz: Royal succession disputes must follow adat, law
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Oct 14 — Disputes over royal succession in Negeri Sembilan must be resolved in accordance with adat or customary law and legal provisions, rather than personal interests, Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir said today. His Royal Highness stressed that the authority of the royal institution must be upheld through integrity, justice and responsibility, warning that actions contrary to established customs could undermine public confidence and threaten the state’s stability. The ceremony was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin.

items.title: Judgment reserved in Saifuddin Nasution’s appeal over RM600,000 awarded to Sanusi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — The Court of Appeal today reserved its judgment in Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail’s appeal against the Alor Setar High Court decision ordering him to pay RM600,000 in damages to Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor for defamation. A three-member bench led by Judge Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli deferred its decision after hearing submissions from Saifuddin Nasution’s counsel Razlan Hadri Zulkifli and counsel Yusfarizal Yussoff, who represented Muhammad Sanusi. On Aug 24, 2025, the Alor Setar High Court allowed Muhammad Sanusi’s suit against Saifuddin Nasution after finding the latter liable for defamation.

items.title: Creative content drive must be matched by child online safety measures, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Efforts to promote creative content on digital platforms must go hand in hand with measures to protect children from online sexual crimes, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. “We want to encourage the production of creative content, including on platforms such as YouTube. Fahmi said the Communications Ministry and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) continued to encourage creative content production, including on digital platforms, as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s creative economy.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan JPJ impounds four luxury cars driven by unlicensed foreigners
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 14 —The Negeri Sembilan Road Transport Department (JPJ) seized four luxury vehicles driven by non-citizens under Op Luxury PeWA, an operation targeting foreign drivers who violate road transport laws. State JPJ director Jasyindar Singh Sihdu said the vehicles comprised a Toyota Vellfire, two Mercedes-Benz A250s and a BMW limousine, driven by Bangladeshi, Pakistani, Chinese and Myanmar nationals aged between 30 and 40. Of the vehicles seized, 313 were motorcycles, 149 were cars and 36 were goods vehicles.

items.title: Police arrest 29 men over alleged spread of banned groups’ propaganda on social media
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Police have arrested 29 men, including a foreigner, on suspicion of promoting and spreading propaganda related to illegal organisations on social media. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects, aged 18 to 49, were arrested under Ops Mega TikTok 2026, conducted from Oct 10-12. “As a result of the operation, involving 11 police contingents in Selangor, Johor, Pahang, Penang, Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Kedah, Melaka, Sabah and Sarawak, 28 Malaysians and a foreigner were arrested,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Police: BYD driver to be charged over fatal Jalan Kuching crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The driver of a BYD Seal involved in a six-vehicle collision that killed a five-year-old girl on Jalan Kuching is to be charged at the Magistrates Court tomorrow. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the investigation team arrested the 24-year-old suspect immediately after he was discharged from a private hospital, where he had sought treatment. Mohd Zamzuri said the suspect would be charged under Sections 41(1), 42(1) and 52(1) of the Road Transport Act for causing death by dangerous or reckless driving, dangerous or reckless driving, and failing to stop after an accident, respectively.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz: Customs cannot be defended by breaching the rules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir today said customs cannot be defended by breaking the very rules of custom, in a pointed address directed at those who have disputed the rules of succession in recent months. Speaking at Istana Besar Seri Menanti this afternoon to mark the investiture of the 17th Undang of Luak Jelebu, Tuanku Muhriz said Negeri Sembilan’s constitutional monarchy, adat and legal provisions must be upheld together. Disputes must follow custom and law The Yamtuan further said the customary system must continue to be strengthened to remain relevant with the times, without neglecting its founding principles and rules.

items.title: Public Services Commission awaits circular on RM2,500 starting salary for fresh grads entering public service
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 14 — The implementation of the RM2,500 starting salary for fresh graduates entering the public service, announced in Budget 2027, is pending an official circular outlining the implementation details. Malaysian Public Services Commission (SPA) chairman and Judicial and Legal Service Commission (SPKP) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the details would include the implementation timeline and related payment components. Asked whether the RM2,500 amount included other allowances, Ahmad Jailani said the matter would be reviewed and clarified in the official circular.

items.title: Malaysia gives Nepal US$1m in flood relief aid
items.summary: Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan presented the contribution to Nepal’s Chargé d’Affaires in Kuala Lumpur, Mudita Bajracharya, at a ceremony here on Wednesday, according to the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra. “The contribution reflects Malaysia’s unwavering support for the government and people of Nepal during this difficult time,” Wisma Putra said in a statement. “The new ordinance will provide greater legal and administrative certainty for affected families,” Wisma Putra said.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang to reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Pahang will reopen tomorrow. The Selangor State Education Department said school operations in the state will prioritise the safety, health and well-being of pupils and school staff. The Melaka State Education Department said educational institutions under MOE will resume operations tomorrow, pending official confirmation of the latest API readings.

items.title: Parliament’s new service council to be fully operational by December, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker
items.summary: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the council would oversee matters including the service scheme, career paths and administration of parliamentary officers, as well as ensure compliance with the provisions of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025. The event was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Dewan Negara President Senator Datuk Seri Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The four appointees, comprising two government and two opposition representatives, are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu).

items.title: Weather warning: MetMalaysia puts most of the country on thunderstorm alert
items.summary: Perak faces widespread disruption across Kerian, Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, and Bagan Datuk. Across Selangor, the warning blankets Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Hulu Langat, and Sepang. Across East Malaysia, the warning stretches across multiple divisions in Sarawak.

items.title: Nhaveen murder trial: Prosecution cites contradictions in four accused’s defence
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 14 — The High Court here was told today that there are four main grounds for the prosecution’s bid to convict the four accused in the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen nine years ago, with the contention that the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt against its case. Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Amril Johari said among these grounds was the contradiction between the defence’s version during the prosecution’s case and the accused’s testimony at the defence stage last week. “The defence’s case at the prosecution stage is totally different from the defence now.

items.title: Five govt buildings get solar installations ahead of schedule, says works minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Five grid-connected photovoltaic (GCPV) solar installation projects at government buildings have been completed ahead of schedule, with a combined installed capacity of 779.86 kilowatts, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said. He said the Public Works Department (JKR) had also implemented grid-connected photovoltaic and off-grid solar installations involving 46 Federal Government buildings, 283 rural schools in Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, four Royal Malaysia Police border posts and an Orang Asli village. As of last September, eight projects involving 23 buildings with a capacity of 5.8 megawatts had completed their Defects Liability Period (DLP), while seven projects involving 11 buildings with a capacity of 2.09 megawatts remained within the period.

items.title: Sarawak Education Dept: Schools open tomorrow, outdoor activities halted if API tops 100
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 14 — All schools and educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Sarawak will operate as usual tomorrow, despite the ongoing haze affecting several areas in the state. In a statement today, the Sarawak Education Department (JPN) said schools in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeded 100 must suspend all outdoor activities. “Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure amid the current haze situation.

items.title: Why should a good man go when the corrupt stay? Anwar says Malaysia needs ministers like Anthony Loke
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim sought again today to make a case for Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook to remain in his Cabinet, saying the country needs principled leaders and that the corrupt should be the ones stepping down. Speaking at the Transport Ministry during the distribution of RM1,000 special financial assistance to taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers, Anwar commended Loke's dedication to ordinary working Malaysians, including the initiative today. Loke, who is the DAP secretary-general, tendered his resignation as transport minister on September 19 following the political controversy surrounding the conditional royal pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

items.title: MACC: Fighting corruption starts with rejecting bribes, reporting misconduct
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Deputy Chief Commissioner (Prevention) Datuk Azmi Kamaruzaman said building a corruption-free culture starts with honest decisions and firm personal convictions, supported by sustained commitment from all parties. He was speaking at the launch of the “Program Langkah Merdeka 118, Bersama Perangi Rasuah” programme, held in conjunction with the MACC’s 59th anniversary celebration for Kuala Lumpur at Stadium Merdeka here today. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib said the symbolic act of carrying and hoisting the MACC flag atop Merdeka 118, Malaysia’s tallest building and the world’s second tallest, reflected the commission’s determination to elevate the anti-corruption agenda and strengthen integrity without compromise.

items.title: Paddy farmers who suffered yield losses from fertiliser delays may get targeted aid, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government will assess whether to provide targeted assistance to paddy farmers whose yields declined due to delays in fertiliser supplies, evaluating affected cases on a case-by-case basis. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the assessment would identify farmers who genuinely suffered losses before considering any assistance. In a separate development, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said 10 per cent of the funds collected through the Warriors’ Fund Campaign (KTP) had been allocated for investment in fixed deposits with financial institutions.

items.title: Foreign minister: Malaysians in Riyadh, Jeddah safe amid Saudi tensions
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysians living and working in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, have been reported safe amid continuing tensions in the country, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. He said daily reports from the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh and the Malaysian Consulate in Jeddah confirmed that Malaysians in both cities were safe and well. He said the security situation in Saudi Arabia remained tense following another reported attack yesterday.
